newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen says looks at international growth.
newsitem.headline: Loewen says looks at international growth.

text.p: The Loewen Group Inc, North America's second-biggest funeral home operator, said Thursday that it may pursue acquisitions abroad.
"We're at a point now where we can once again look at international opportunities, which we are doing," chief executive Ray Loewen told the company's annual meeting.
The company made a bid for Great Southern Group of Britain in 1994 but was defeated by its arch-rival Service Corp International.
Houston-based Service bills itself as the world's biggest funeral and cemetery chain with operations in France, Britain, Australia and elsewhere.
Loewen declined to say which countries his company was targeting for acquisitions. Loewen's operations are currently confined to the United States and Canada.
The company is "monitoring" two or three prospects but has "nothing specific" in the works, Loewen said.

Loewen decided in 1995 to focus solely on the North American market because it felt this was less risky than venturing further afield. Since then it has grown rapidly by buying up independent cemeteries and funeral homes.
